heroHeadline: South Korea Voices Regret Over Ukraine's Denial of North Korean POW Pact as DPRK Troops Deployment Triggers Diplomatic Fallout
heroSubtitle: South Korea expressed regret on September 27, 2026 after Ukraine denied a reported agreement on handling North Korean prisoners of war captured during the Russia-Ukraine war, underscoring deepening diplomatic friction over the DPRK's troop deployment to Russia. Earlier, KCNA confirmed North Korea's September 20 double short-range ballistic missile launch tested an upgraded hypersonic-glide warhead, with Kim Jong-un calling it an 'incurable headache' for adversaries. Foreign Minister Choe Son-hui declared on September 24 that North Korea's nuclear status is 'irreversible... and will remain unchanged forever.'
footerNote: Data sourced from US/ROK official reports, KCNA, UN panels, IAEA, and institutional analyses. North Korea does not publish national statistics — economic figures are estimates with wide uncertainty ranges.
